name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
explanation: This criterion applies to prerecorded video that has an audio track — for example, a product demo, a training video, or a film with dialogue. If the video conveys important information visually that isn't already spoken in the dialogue, like on-screen text or a character's silent action, you must provide one of two things: an audio description track that narrates those visual details during pauses in the dialogue, or a full text or media alternative that describes everything happening in both the video and audio. This is about giving access to the visual half of the video, not the audio half — captions solve the opposite problem, making the audio accessible to people who can't hear it. If a video's dialogue already explains everything visually important as it happens, no separate audio description is needed.
whoItAffects: Blind users and people with low vision who use screen readers, or simply can't see the screen well enough to follow visual-only content, depend on audio description or a full alternative to know what's happening. Without it, they hear the soundtrack and dialogue but miss plot points, on-screen instructions, or data shown only as an image or chart — like a demo where a presenter silently clicks through a UI, or a scene where a character reads a letter on screen with no narration. People with cognitive disabilities benefit from having visual events narrated aloud. Users on a shared or low-bandwidth connection who load a text alternative instead of streaming video also benefit from this content being available.

codeExample.bad:
<!-- Silent software demo: presenter clicks through settings with no narration of what's on screen -->
<video controls width="640" height="360">
  <source src="settings-walkthrough.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="captions" src="settings-walkthrough-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
codeExample.good: Read the full text alternative, which describes every on-screen action and setting change.

howToTest: Watch each prerecorded video with your eyes closed and listen only to the audio track. Note every point where something happens visually that isn't described in words — a silent gesture, on-screen text, a chart, a character entering a room. Then check whether the video offers a narrated audio description track that fills those gaps, or whether a full text alternative is linked nearby that describes the same visual information. It fails if neither exists and you noticed visual gaps while listening.

check.question: A prerecorded training video shows a narrator silently pointing at different parts of a diagram while soft background music plays, with no spoken explanation of what she's pointing to. What does SC 1.2.3 require in this case?
choices: Nothing, because the video already has captions for the music
An audio description track (or full text alternative) that conveys what's being pointed at, since that information is only available visually
A sign-language interpreter inset in the video
Increasing the video's color contrast so the diagram is easier to see
